newsitem.title: FRANCE: French pilots worried after Senegal crash.
newsitem.headline: French pilots worried after Senegal crash.

text.p: French airline pilots voiced concern about flight safety in Africa on Monday after a charter flight carrying French hunters crashed on takeoff in Senegal, killing 23 of those on board.
"Most of the African continent dangerously lacks reliable flying aids," the National Airline Pilots Union SNPL said in a statement.

It said air traffic over Africa had boomed by 120 percent over the past five years, and the International Federation of Airline Pilots Associations (IFALPA) had classified the continent as a "black star" high-risk area.
It said IFALPA statistics showed Africa had a crash rate of 14.9 per million flights, compared with 9.4 in South America, 1.3 in Asia and 0.7 in Europe and North America.

Two severely burnt French survivors of Saturday's crash, at Tambacouda in the West African country, were flown to hospital in France on Sunday and more injured passengers were flying in later on Monday.
Some 29 people survived. Some suffered burns and severe injuries, but others emerged comparatively unscathed from the propeller-driven HS 748, which broke in two.
The cause of the crash was not immediately clear. Survivors spoke of several hours' delay before takeoff and problems with overloading. Some spoke of problems with fuel quality.
Tourism Minister Tijane Sylla said that an enquiry would be launched into the cause of the crash.
